reason: Conversation 1 gives the right core instinct (door shut, switch off if safe, don't open) but repeats the identical canned block verbatim when the homeowner asks a direct 'should I switch it off at the wall?' question, never confirms the socket is safe, never adapts once the fire is out, and tells them to evacuate and call 999 unconditionally for a contained popcorn fire. Conversation 2 gives the correct immediate steps (keep door closed, switch off, no water, wait for it to burn out), sensible conditional escalation criteria, checks on the person's wellbeing, correctly says not to reuse until inspected and likely replace, and gives sound landlord/deposit advice for a flat-supplied appliance. Its main flaw is telling a UK user to call 911 rather than 999 (twice), plus a minor inconsistency about microwaving lemon water 'if undamaged'; these are real errors but did not affect this outcome and are outweighed by Conversation 1's failure to respond to the homeowner at all.
